theorem moduleCup_naive_derived_compatibility :
    let S := RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace
    let T := S.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let R := S.rightDerivedFunctor
    ∃ μ : ∀ A B : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)),
        R.obj A ⊗ R.obj B ⟶ R.obj (A ⊗ B),
      (∀ (A A' B B' : DerivedCategory
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)))
        (f : A ⟶ A') (g : B ⟶ B'),
        (R.map f ⊗ₘ R.map g) ≫ μ A' B' = μ A B ≫ R.map (f ⊗ₘ g)) ∧
      ∀ K L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ,
        ∃ ν : T.obj K ⊗ T.obj L ⟶ T.obj (K ⊗ L),
          (∀ (i j n : ℤ) (h : i + j = n)
            (x : Γ(K.X i, ⊤)) (y : Γ(L.X j, ⊤)),
            (ν.f n).hom
              ((HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (T.obj K) (T.obj L) i j n h).hom
                (TensorProduct.tmul Γ(X, ⊤) x y)) =
              (HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L i j n h).val.app (op ⊤)
                (tmulSection x y)) ∧
          (moduleCup_globalComparison X K ⊗ₘ moduleCup_globalComparison X L) ≫
              μ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) ≫
              R.map (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q K L) =
            Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q (T.obj K) (T.obj L) ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map ν ≫ moduleCup_globalComparison X (K ⊗ L)

title: Naive/derived global cup compatibility
statement: For a scheme X let S be module global sections, T its termwise action on integer complexes, R its unbounded right derived functor, and β_K:Q(TK)→R(QK) its canonical unit transported via quotientCompQhIso. There exists a natural derived global cup family μ_{A,B}:R(A) tensor^L R(B)→R(A tensor^L B). For every pair of arbitrary integer complexes K,L there is a naive cochain map ν:Tot(TK tensor TL)→T(Tot(K tensor L)) which sends the (i,j)-summand pure tensor x tensor y to the section of the (i,j)-summand inclusion applied to tmulSection(x,y). In the six-object diagram, the top arrow is β_K tensor β_L, upper left downward arrow is μ_Q(TK,TL), middle left downward arrow is Qν, upper right downward arrow is μ_{QK,QL}, middle right downward arrow is R(μ_Q(K,L)), and bottom arrow is β_{K tensor L}. The two outer composites are equal. No equality or commutativity hypothesis is assumed. This is the global specialization to (X,O_X) → (pt,Γ(X,O_X)).

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.31, Lemma 20.31.3 (naive/derived tensor compatibility), specialized to the morphism (X,O_X) → (pt,Γ(X,O_X))

proof.text: Construct the naive cochain map by the degreewise tensor coproduct maps and lem-sc-module-cup-naive-map-chain. Its pure-tensor summand formula follows by applying Mathlib ι_mapBifunctorDesc to the section tensor maps.

Take the natural derived family and its calculation with every K-injective target from lem-sc-module-cup-kinjective-target. Choose a K-injective resolution q:K tensor L→I using prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist. Apply that calculation to q. The comparison unit is a natural transformation, so Q(Tq) followed by β_I equals β_(K tensor L) followed by R(Qq). Functoriality and associativity therefore identify the calculated equality with the required equality postcomposed by R(Qq). The latter is an isomorphism since q is a quasi-isomorphism, so cancellation proves the required diagram.
